task.instruction: Choose exactly one authority mode for the next seven days: basin-desk scheduling or district-controlled permits. Hybrid authority is unavailable. State the volume boundary, expiry, safety interlock, and conflict rule. Cite the supplied evidence IDs.

evidence.content: There are three irrigation districts; District C's six-megaliter pulse reduced crop-canopy temperature by 22%.
Downstream turbidity p95 rose 46% and two municipal intake windows were missed during the pulse.
The basin has 30 megaliters available; one district may release at most two megaliters; permits expire after 15 minutes; the cap is hard and gates close within 90 seconds.

Four two-megaliter trials reduced crop-canopy temperature by 9%, kept downstream turbidity within 4% of baseline, and missed no intake windows. An automatic interlock closes every gate if turbidity reaches 10% above baseline.
The basin allocation table refreshes every four hours; districts see soil moisture and canal flow live.

The control system can run exactly one mode for seven days: the basin desk schedules and resolves every release, or districts use preallocated permits and the earliest signed request resolves conflicts. In district mode the basin desk can observe and the safety interlock can close gates, but neither can reallocate or preapprove a release.
A surgical campus had 24 recovery slots; one ward's five-slot extension raised other-ward waits 31% and delayed two procedures.
A charging cooperative used a hard 60-kilowatt ceiling, local live demand meters, and 10-minute leases with no feeder spillover for eight weeks.

nondiagnostic_target_a.content: 2026-04-16 — Decision: Route recovery-slot extensions through the campus desk. Reason: A five-slot local gain raised other waits 31% and delayed two procedures. Evidence: [rb-s3d-prior-01].
2026-05-14 — Decision: Leave charging leases with members under the 60-kilowatt ceiling. Reason: Live meters and 10-minute leases produced eight spillover-free weeks. Evidence: [rb-s3d-prior-02].

nondiagnostic_target_b.content: 2026-04-16 — Decision: Let wards exchange one temporary slot under a campus ceiling. Reason: Local discharge evidence is current while the 31% wait cost remains bounded. Evidence: [rb-s3d-prior-01].
2026-05-14 — Decision: Review charging allocations centrally each morning. Reason: Eight quiet weeks do not remove shared accountability for the 60-kilowatt feeder. Evidence: [rb-s3d-prior-02].
